narrative:
The model estimates a 68% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors about your situation.

The strongest influence is that you have received other job opportunities while working here. Having external offers is a major signal that you may be considering leaving, and this factor pushed the prediction most strongly toward departure.

Next, your six to ten years of experience in your current role worked in your favor. Most employees predicted to stay have only one to five years here, so your longer tenure in this organization pulled the prediction back toward staying. Similarly, your overall career experience of six to ten years also nudged the outcome slightly toward leaving, though this effect was smaller than the pull from external opportunities.

Taken together, the combination of having other job offers outweighed the stabilizing effect of your time with the company, leading to the decision to deny the promotion.

Your organization should discuss retention strategies with you, such as addressing any unmet needs that might be making external offers attractive. You may want to reflect on whether those opportunities better align with your goals and openly share your career aspirations with your manager.
